summary: Ishtar is a tight, puzzly rondel-and-tile-placement game where you plant flowers to trigger chained bonuses, then race to claim gem-based scoring conditions before opponents beat you to them. Turns are quick but the board state is tense, since good flower placements are contested and trees can cut off your opponents' combos.
praised: Clever, tight rondel mechanism that constrains choices meaningfully
Fast turns keep the game moving despite the thinking involved
Good player count scalability, plays well at 2
criticised: Can feel a bit dry or abstract despite the gardening theme
Some player interaction is more about racing/blocking than direct engagement, which can feel solitaire-ish at times
Upgrade/gem economy can be hard to parse for new players
Limited replayability variance once strategies are known

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via tree placement and racing for gem thresholds

scoring.why: Points come from trees, apprentice scoring in flower copses, and upgrade bonuses, but efficient combo-chaining on the rondel decides the winner
